claims.rationale: Only classical exact and controlled sampled simulations were run; the frozen manifest explicitly makes no quantum-advantage claim.
The point estimates contradict this: logistic regression leads financial macro-F1, GARCH leads QLIKE, ESN leads RMSE and MNIST.

claims.claim: QRC was competitive with ESN for financial classification.
claims.rationale: QRC and ESN point estimates are close and none of macro-F1, balanced accuracy or transition PR-AUC differed after Holm correction. Competitive does not mean superior or equivalent.

claims.claim: QRC significantly outperformed regime persistence for transition PR-AUC.
claims.rationale: The architecture-level paired interval is positive and the Holm-adjusted p-value is below 0.05.

claims.claim: Logistic regression significantly outperformed QRC on financial macro-F1.
claims.rationale: The QRC-minus-logistic interval is negative and the Holm-adjusted p-value is 0.0168.

claims.claim: GARCH achieved the best test QLIKE.
claims.rationale: GARCH has the lowest frozen test QLIKE point estimate in the directly comparable table.

claims.claim: ESN achieved the best test RMSE.
claims.rationale: ESN has the lowest frozen test RMSE point estimate.

claims.claim: QRC produced the highest architecture-level variance correlation.
claims.rationale: The mean across the three frozen QRC seeds is 0.543, above the directly comparable ESN, GARCH and persistence correlations.

claims.claim: QRC and flattened logistic were statistically indistinguishable on MNIST after Holm correction.
claims.rationale: No tested MNIST metric was Holm-significant, but failure to reject is not an equivalence or non-inferiority result.

claims.claim: ESN significantly outperformed QRC on MNIST.
claims.rationale: All four architecture-level MNIST comparisons favour ESN after Holm correction.

claims.claim: A reliable transition lead time was demonstrated.
claims.rationale: Lead time is not identifiable from the frozen aggregate target rows; no forecast-origin/target/transition-date mapping exists.

claims.claim: The finite-shot simulations represent physical QPU performance.
claims.rationale: The frozen execution manifest records no physical-QPU execution.

claims.claim: Increasing the number of qubits monotonically improved validation performance.
claims.rationale: Validation macro-F1, transition PR-AUC and QLIKE vary non-monotonically over two to six qubits.
No improvement hypothesis was tested; non-monotonic simulation changes are treated only as stochastic/model variability.
